data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's calibration signature is not a valid way to distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance within a single evaluation. A panel can exhibit monotonic confidence/agreement that is perfectly correlated with evidence clarity even when merely mechanically following the checklist; in fact, a well-specified checklist will produce higher agreement on clear cases and lower agreement on ambiguous ones as a mechanical byproduct. This signature tracks checklist determinacy, not genuine reliability. Counterexample: a panel blindly following a flawed checklist will show monotonic confidence based solely on item-match count—producing the exact calibration curve described—without any genuine reliability gain. The target also conflates 'frequentist justification' with reliability, ignoring that a checklist can be reproducibly wrong.
